mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate indicates easy monetary policy, which may stimulate investment and consumption, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 60% of the 20-day periods following low FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day periods following a UNRATE increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate coupled with low unemployment indicates a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods with high FEDFUNDS and low UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer price index during a late-cycle expansion may lead to tighter monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day periods following CPI increases in late-cycle, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth indicates a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day periods following GDP growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in industrial production suggests supply chain issues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day periods following INDPRO declines, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth coupled with increased retail sales indicates a robust economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods with strong PAYEMS and RSAFS growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts in an early-cycle recovery indicates economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of the 60-day periods following HOUST growth in early-cycle recovery, the hypothesis is rejected.
